verdict.reasoning: Patient states a “blinding headache for a few days” and reports difficulty working: “it's…really bothering me and I find it very hard to focus or like I can't even go to work.” Duration clarified as three days later: “that was three days ago.”

Onset and course: “It just started all of a sudden. I woke up one morning with a headache, and that was three days ago. And I just keep having. It doesn't really go away without ibuprofen either.” This supports sudden onset and continuous 3‑day duration.

Analgesic response and severity: patient rates pain “mostly eight, and then it comes down to maybe a five” and says ibuprofen “gets a little bit better, but doesn't go away,” consistent with partial relief from 8/10 to about 5/10.
Location: “It's kind of all over, but I feel like over. My right eye is a bit stronger.” This describes a diffuse headache worse over the right eye.
Photophobia: In response to light sensitivity question, patient says, “Lights definitely make me more sensitive. I don't really like strong lights,” consistent with photophobia.

Visual phenomena: patient reports, “yeah, vision. I think I get this shooting light sometimes. Not sure how to explain it. Just a bit of a weird kind of vision,” which matches intermittent shooting light visual phenomena.
Nausea without vomiting: to nausea/vomiting query, patient says, “No, I'm feeling a bit sick, but no vomiting,” indicating nausea/feeling sick without vomiting.
Focal deficits: to “Any tingling or numbness or weakness anywhere?” patient answers, “No,” denying focal numbness or weakness.

Fever: later discussion notes, “But you haven't had a high temperature. Have you checked your temperature?” Patient replies, “No, I didn't, but I don't really feel feverish or anything.” This supports denial of fever.
URI symptoms: clinician asks about “cold symptoms, sore throat, sore ears…or phlegm, any nosebleeds or cough,” and patient responds, “No,” denying recent upper respiratory symptoms.
Nasal/sinus: same question includes “pain over the sinuses…any nosebleeds,” and patient answers, “No,” which denies nasal or sinus symptoms.

Positional/stabbing: patient says, “Sometimes when I stand up quickly, I get a bit of a stabbing pain or if I turn my head, I kind of feel like something is moving inside,” supporting worsening with quick standing or head turning as brief stabbing pain.

Sleep: patient confirms, “Yeah, I'm sleeping,” and when asked if it wakes them at night: “No, no, but I can wake up with it in the morning.” This indicates able to sleep, wakes with headache, not nocturnally disruptive.
Eye check: “Yeah, actually had one recently and nothing changed my vision,” consistent with a recent normal eye check.
Past medical history: “I think I only had the abdominal pain when I was younger, but no cause was found and that went away,” describing remote childhood abdominal pain without diagnosis.
Contraceptive: “Just the pill.” When asked which, “Marcelone.” Start time: “About a year ago.” Combined pill is implied by context of BP check and migraine discussion.
Ibuprofen use: “apart from the ibuprofen I take sometimes and the headache gets really bad,” indicating occasional ibuprofen use.
Allergies: to “And any allergies to anything?” patient answers, “No,” indicating no known allergies.
Family history: patient states, “my mum suffers from…she has migraines…She's like. Has the vomiting and everything,” which matches maternal migraines with vomiting.
Living situation: to “Who do you live with at home?” patient answers, “Just by myself,” indicating living alone.
Smoking: to “And do you smoke?” patient replies, “No,” confirming non‑smoker status.
Alcohol: to “How much in a normal week?” patient says, “Probably like three beers once a Week,” matching the stated consumption.
Drugs: clinician asks, “And do you take any other drugs at all?” Patient responds, “No, apart from the ibuprofen I take sometimes,” denying recreational drug use.
The transcript contains no physical examination maneuvers or objective findings; only history and plan are discussed, so stating that no exam findings are documented is accurate.

Clinician assessment: acknowledges acute severe headache for three days with visual symptoms and photophobia and need for exam: “it could possibly be a migraine type headache, but it's ongoing for three days. We probably should book you into an appointment to get an examination…we should do a neurological examination, look at the back of your eyes as well.” This supports probable migraine phenotype and need to exclude secondary causes with neuro exam and fundoscopy.

Pill relevance: “When you have an examination with us, we'll check your blood pressure as well, just to make sure your pill is still appropriate for you. Because if we do think it's a migraine, then you would have to change your pill…If you've had these flashing lights.” This ties combined pill (Marcelone) to migraine with aura and BP check/medication review.

Functional impairment: patient says headache makes it hard to focus and work, and describes missed/limited work: “I work from home, but couldn't really manage to do it all the time…second day I just do the whole day off…today I just tried to work…stopped in the morning because I couldn't focus.”

Plan: “we probably should book you into an appointment to get an examination…we should do a neurological examination, look at the back of your eyes as well.” Later: “When you have an examination with us, we'll check your blood pressure as well.” This supports an in‑person appointment for neuro exam, fundoscopy, and BP check.

Medication plan: “I can prescribe you something similar to ibuprofen, but a bit stronger, which you can take instead of ibuprofen, and you can take paracetamol at the same time. … take it with food,” supporting a stronger NSAID‑type analgesic plus concurrent paracetamol with food.

OCP continuation/review: clinician explains pill may need changing if migraine with aura, then says, “All right, but you can carry on with that for the moment,” matching advice to continue Marcelone for now and reassess if migraine with aura confirmed.

Safety‑netting: “if in the meantime, before your appointment, your headache is getting unbearable, getting worse or changing, then if it's that bad, then you should go to AE and have an examination. You can call us for further advice on that.” While focal signs are not explicitly mentioned, the advice to attend emergency if worsening/unbearable headache is clearly given; the additional phrase about “new focal neurologic signs” is an implied standard but not literally stated, so this introduces new detail.
Cancellation if improved: “Obviously, if it settles in the meantime, then we can cancel that,” referring to the planned appointment.

Follow‑up plan restates plan‑001 and plan‑005: in‑person examination for neurology/fundoscopy/BP (“book you into an appointment…neurological examination, look at the back of your eyes…we'll check your blood pressure as well”) with instruction to cancel if it settles (“if it settles in the meantime, then we can cancel that”).

ROS elements: patient denies feeling feverish (“I don't really feel feverish or anything”), denies numbness/weakness (“Any tingling or numbness or weakness anywhere? – No.”), and denies URI/nasal/sinus symptoms in response to the cold/sinus/nosebleed question (“No.”).
